title: Slovakia Caught Between Austerity Backlash and Persistent Inflation · 11 Sep
keywords: Slovakia, Robert Fico, inflation, GDP growth, fiscal consolidation, austerity, eurozone, European Commission, budget deficit, cost of living, protests, National Bank of Slovakia, central Europe, EU fiscal rules
notes: Slovakia is navigating one of its most difficult economic periods in recent memory, with inflation still running well above the euro-area average and GDP growth stuck below one percent for six consecutive quarters. Prime Minister Robert Fico's government is pressing ahead with fiscal consolidation to rein in a deficit that Brussels considers dangerously wide, but the measures are drawing large protests and deepening public anger. The country has become a test case for how a small eurozone economy can manage simultaneous pressures of weak growth, stubborn prices, and politically charged budget cuts.
